own_solution.law: Energy conservation in an insulated calorimeter: m_w c (dT0 - T) = m_i L + m_i c T, with T the final temperature above the melting point; heat given up Q = m_w c (dT0 - T)
assumptions: all ice melts (checked: T = 23.48 K above melting > 0)

notes: Base: 0.5*4186*(40-T) = 0.08*334000 + 0.08*4186*T -> T = 57000/2427.88 = 23.4773 K above melting; Q = 34582.07 J. With the first-container water heated 17 K before ice is added (start 57 K above): T = 92581/2427.88 = 38.1324 K; Q = 26720 + 334.88*38.1324 = 39489.80 J (heat given up measured from the temperature at which ice is added). T96AB 'the water' is read as the first-container water (the base says the water is poured into the first container). T2F5B and T162D state 'a few kelvin' rather than 17 K; as distractors this does not change the answer, but they do not state the same number as their 17 K variants. Earlier-run sentences refer to a different run and are disconnected.
